name: nofp
description: FP trap stubs and the libm wrap surface for FPU-less guests
note: The zkVM platforms link these wraps. The stock musl target also links module.o (bflat.csproj puts a copy in lib/linux/riscv64/musl), but without the wraps.

wrap.note: libm: divert the transcendental functions that the runtime references (MathHelpers.cpp RhpDbl* helpers, GC allocation sampling) to the nofp trap stubs. The bundled musl is built rv64im, so its implementations would link and run correctly - the point is that a transcendental has no business inside a proof, and a guest that reaches one is a bug worth hearing about. The exact operations are deliberately NOT here: ceil, floor, modf, sqrt, fma, scalbn and fmod have one correctly rounded IEEE 754 result, like + and /, and musl computes them with integer arithmetic. CoreLib calls them for ordinary work (double formatting, DateTime.Add*, HashHelpers.IsPrime).

asprintf is referenced only by the PAL's CGroup CPU-limit parsing, which cannot open its /proc and /sys inputs on a zkVM (pal's open() returns -1). The stub returns -1, the documented asprintf failure, so the path degrades to no cgroup limit. It also keeps musl's vasprintf and the float formatter of vfprintf out of the image.
